blocked_until: physical cleanup is executed and re-verified

corrected_ontology_definitions.Extended_AMR: an extension of AMR's own ontological space, plus a graph encoding of concrete events, entities and roles bound to canonical ontology items. A carrier candidate, not a competitor to KEOL.
corrected_ontology_definitions.KEOL: a method for dynamic ontology construction. It turns unmapped expressions into candidate concepts, operators and senses, then normalizes, deduplicates, detects conflicts, admits or rejects, and versions the result. It is not a representation format.
corrected_ontology_definitions.ontology: a versioned namespace of stable ids, senses, aliases, types, relations and constraints. Loosely a controlled vocabulary, but a bare string set is not one: without ids and senses there is nothing for a mapping to be correct or incorrect about.

seed_sources.note: these are candidate ontology or vocabulary/schema sources. None is expected to carry a complete ontology alone.

current_status_bounds.accurate_description: ontology-first memory prototype with hand-authored semantic diagnostics, candidate carrier conformance and partial automatic proposal experiments
forbidden_descriptions: A-D controlled results as benchmark results or product superiority
proven: Phase C: narrow-vocabulary qualification on its own contract
Phase D: one controlled production-contract write-to-query closure
evidence chain: revision -> span -> raw turn, with Git snapshot recovery

data_flow: L1 ontology mapping -> O_L1 | unresolved -> KEOL proposal/admission
L2 abstraction over L1 units and raw evidence
L2 ontology mapping -> O_L2 | unresolved -> KEOL proposal/admission
carrier materialization (KE triples | Extended AMR | typed graph | other)
query compilation against O_L1, O_L2 or an explicit cross-layer bridge
symbolic execution, then guarded embedding fallback
failure_protocol_rules: every failed attempt is preserved immutably
never overwrite a run root to make it look successful
never tune prompts, edit gold or relax the scorer against hidden results
report raw quality and gate intervention separately; a gate stop is not model quality

freezes: seed source versions (WordNet, schema.org, PropBank, domain lists)
gates.name: freeze inputs and identities
L1 closed-world ontology mapping
gates.ontology: O_L1 frozen, no dynamic extension permitted
gates.rule: L1 is scored alone; no L2 or carrier result may mask an L1 failure

measures: conflict, update, time and identity handling
gates.name: L2 separate-ontology abstraction
gates.rule: report L2 raw abstraction quality, L2 mapping quality, derivation correctness and evidence closure separately. L1 accuracy may never stand in for L2 accuracy.

gates.dev: KEOL may propose new concepts, operators, senses and relations
gates.hidden: only the ontology version frozen before the run may be read
measures: benefit and side effects on later L1/L2/query
gates.name: KEOL dynamic ontology track
gates.rule: the model proposes; it never writes the canonical ontology directly

gates.held_fixed: O_L1, O_L2 and the cross-layer map
gates.name: carrier conformance
gates.rule: no carrier is pre-selected; only one passing the hard gate proceeds

gates.name: query and retrieval
gates.rule: embedding may close lexical, entity and evidence gaps only. It may not stand in for ontology sense, time, negation, conflict or L2 closure.

annotation_rules: LongMemEval oracle-haystack results marked separately and never generalized to full retrieval
gates.name: natural-language end to end

slice.note: the existing 32-item slice is dev/regression only and may never be reused as fresh hidden. A formal end-to-end run needs new fresh hidden.

layer_ontology_rule: O_L1 and O_L2 may be entirely different, partly shared, or connected only through a declared derivation map. Each is versioned and hashed separately. A shared vocabulary must never be assumed by default -- that assumption is what an independent l1_ontology_sha256, l2_ontology_sha256 and cross_layer_map_sha256 exist to prevent.
mapping_rule: an unmapped expression never becomes a canonical item directly. It enters KEOL construction and only reaches the ontology through admission, so a new phrasing cannot silently grow a new operator.

primary_metrics.ambiguity_rate: share resolved to more than one candidate sense
primary_metrics.canonical_sense_accuracy: correct sense given a correct concept
primary_metrics.error_propagation_rate: how often a mapping error changes the evidence set, the constraint or the answer -- the measure of whether mapping errors matter downstream
primary_metrics.false_merge_rate: distinct referents collapsed into one item
primary_metrics.mapping_coverage: share of surface expressions reaching a canonical item
primary_metrics.mis_mapping_rate: share mapped to the wrong item -- scored separately from unresolved, because a confident wrong mapping is worse than an honest gap
primary_metrics.note: per the correction, mapping quality is the headline, not end-to-end answer score. A high answer score over a vocabulary that never had to map anything measures very little.
primary_metrics.ontology_version_consistency: items stable across versions where they should be
primary_metrics.query_memory_alignment: query terms and stored terms resolving to the same items

supersedes: the earlier plan, which treated KEOL, Extended AMR and WordNet/schema.org as sibling representation candidates. That conflated three different levels and is withdrawn.
withdrawn_claims: Extended AMR is the primary carrier candidate. Its conformance results show it is *a* viable carrier, not that it should be selected. No carrier is chosen before Gate 4.
KEOL versus Extended AMR is a meaningful comparison. They sit at different levels: one constructs the ontology, the other encodes instances against it.
